findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 PIC went between tasks without washing hands. Orders were prepared and cashed out prior to putting on gloves to prepare another order. Proper handwashing between tasks was discussed. Even if facility is short staffed, handwashing after working the register needs to be a priority before doing any tasks related to food prep/handling, especially before putting on gloves to prepare orders.   
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed upon entering the kitchen, before putting on gloves, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 PIC was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier, and handle of paper towel dispenser was touched to dispense paper towels after hand washing occurred. Proper technique was discussed with staff. Proper handwashing technique poster is located at the handwashing sink for reference.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.citation_text:
3-403.11 Backup portions of potato soup and meatballs had internal temperatures of 120F and 96F-108F respectively. PIC just moved the products to a warmer that was holding tomato soup at 140F. Warmer previously in use was said to be new and may not be working properly but was turned on to heat products during morning prep. PIC noted they were busy and short staffed today and thus didn’t have time to check temperatures prior to service. It would appear the soup and meatballs may have never reached a minimum temperature of 135F and were discarded. 
Ready-to-eat TCS food that has been commercially processed and packaged in a food processing plant that is inspected by the regulatory authority that has jurisdiction over the plant, shall be heated to a temperature of at least 135F when being reheated for hot holding.

3-501.18 1. Portions of vegetarian turkey, roast beef, ham, turkey, and tomatoes in the bottom of the sandwich prep cooler were observed with dates marks showing the last day of use was 2/7. Additional pans of in-use deli meats and tomatoes were also observed with use by dates of 2/7 in the top of the prep cooler. All foods prepared foods with use by dates of 2/7 were discarded during inspection. A few products had a use by date of 2/8 and were immediately put in the cooler to be used or discarded by the end of operations today.
2. Hummus in the bottom of the prep cooler was without a date mark. Manager noted the product was opened Wednesday of last week. Hummus was to be used or discarded by the end of operations today. 
Ensure proper date marking and that all foods are served or discarded by the use by date.
A food specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in ¶ 3501.17(A).

Owner was advised to be careful with overstocking, and products were to be re-portioned so foods were not stocked above ill lines in pans to help maintain colder temperatures. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration

findings.comment: .1360) employee coat found stored on unused bread rack.  Store employee personal items away from food prep/storage areas.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F. Foods observed without proper labels. Mostly foods that came from the commissary. Make sure all foods that are prepared (sliced) are labeled with date and time of prep and help cold in transit. All potentially hazardous foods not in original containers must have labels unless they are used within 24 hours.  Label foods properly

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. A speed rack of bread is stored next to the hand wash sink. Wash water is splattering onto the bags of bread. Move the rack and or provide and impervious cover to the rack. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: 750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user. Store all single use articles protected by arranging the eating surfaces and handles facing in the same direction.  Protect single use items.
